stem:
A 3-week-old has two episodes of green vomiting. He is haemodynamically stable, the abdomen is soft and a plain abdominal radiograph is non-diagnostic.

What is the safest next step?

options.label: A
options.text: Observe in hospital until bilious vomiting recurs
options.explanation: A well interval does not exclude intermittent malrotation with volvulus; waiting risks bowel ischaemia.

options.label: B
options.text: Give oral rehydration solution and repeat the radiograph
options.explanation: Further feeding is unsafe while a mechanical obstruction and volvulus remain possible.

options.label: C
options.text: Seek urgent surgical assessment for bowel obstruction
options.explanation: Bilious vomiting in a young infant can reflect bowel obstruction or midgut volvulus. Surgical assessment is urgent even when the infant looks well and the plain film is non-diagnostic; the team can then coordinate definitive imaging.

options.label: D
options.text: Discharge after a normal ultrasound of the pylorus
options.explanation: A soft abdomen early in volvulus does not make discharge safe.

context: Bilious vomiting in a young infant is malrotation with midgut volvulus until excluded. A stable appearance and non-diagnostic plain film do not remove the need for urgent surgical assessment.
